response.overlap_assessment: Real overlap: you and Daniel both worked at Fictional Advisory Partners (in different years), and he made the exact consulting-to-PM move you're targeting. His leadership of an analytics product group also lines up naturally with your pricing dashboard work and your love of turning messy data into usable tools.
response.outreach_email:
Subject: Fellow Fictional Advisory Partners alum, curious about the move to PM

Hi Daniel,

I'm Priya, a Class of 2028 MBA candidate and former Senior Consultant at Fictional Advisory Partners, so I was glad to see we share that background. I'm hoping to move into product management, and your path from consultant to leading Northwind's analytics product group is the jump I'd like to make. My favorite project was building a pricing dashboard used by 30 store managers.

Would you be open to a 20-minute chat? I'd love to hear how you made the transition and which skills you built first.

Thanks,
Priya
questions: When you left Fictional Advisory Partners after three years to join Northwind as a PM, what actually got you the role: a relationship, a specific type of project, or how you pitched your consulting experience?
Which skills from consulting carried straight into your first PM role, and which did you have to build first?
How did your path go from individual PM to leading the analytics product group, and what changed most about your day-to-day as you made that step?
In analytics products, users often ask for more and more features. How do you decide which requests to build and which to say no to?
If an ex-consultant interviewed for a PM role in your group, what would you want to hear about their client projects to believe they could own a product end to end?

tmay_2min.text: Hi Daniel, thank you so much for taking the time to chat with me.
I'm Priya, and I'm an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028.
My background started on the technical side:
I earned my B.S. in Information Systems in 2021,
and that same year I joined Fictional Advisory Partners.
I know you spent three years there as a consultant,
so I suspect a lot of this will sound familiar.
I was there from 2021 to 2026 as a Senior Consultant, leading four digital transformation projects for retail clients.
The project closest to my heart
was building a pricing dashboard that was used by 30 store managers.
What I remember most is that
the store managers kept asking for more features.
That felt like the best kind of feedback, because it meant the tool was genuinely useful to them.
It also made something click for me:
I love turning messy data into tools people actually use.
That's really why I'm at business school now.
My goal is to move from consulting into product management and own a product end to end,
and I'm focusing on Product Manager roles at B2B software companies.
I'm excited about the idea of sitting closer to users and staying with a product over time, rather than handing it off when a project wraps up.
That's a big part of why I was so eager to talk with you.
You made the move from consulting at Fictional Advisory Partners to a PM role at Northwind Software, and now you lead the analytics product group,
which feels like a path I'd love to learn from.
I'm especially curious
about how you made the jump from consulting to PM and what skills you had to build first.
I'd also love to hear how your consulting instincts show up in your work today.
